chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from al-Harith al-Nasri who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am from a family that has become extinct and there is no child for me.'
He said: 'Supplicate while you are in prostration:'

O Lord! Grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me. O Lord! Grant me from Yourself good offspring; indeed You are the All-Hearing of supplication. O Lord! Do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors.
He said: 'So I did it, and there were born unto me Ali and al-Husayn.'

key_terms.انقرضوا: Became extinct/died out — referring to a family line ending without heirs
key_terms.خير الوارثين: The Best of Inheritors — a divine epithet from Quran 21:89 emphasizing God's ultimate ownership of all
key_terms.ذرية طيبة: Good/pure offspring — a Quranic phrase (3:38) from Zakariyya's supplication
key_terms.ساجد: In a state of prostration (sajda), the position of greatest physical humility before God
key_terms.وليًّا يرثني: An heir who inherits — combining spiritual guardianship with continuation of lineage

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for someone without children?
ai.summary: This hadith records al-Harith al-Nasri's account of consulting Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about his childlessness. The Imam prescribed a specific supplication to be recited during the sacred moment of prostration (sajda), weaving together Quranic phrases from the supplications of prophets Zakariyya (AS) and others (Quran 19:5-6, 3:38, 21:89). The narrator reports that he followed this prescription and was blessed with two sons named Ali and al-Husayn, demonstrating the efficacy of supplication during prostration.
